_preregistration.primary: Spearman between argmax_T V(T) and measured T*, SETTLED ensemble, gated by gatecheck.leverage.correlation_leverage (predictor must span >= half the target)
_preregistration.secondary: do the no-finite-T* models have a systematically different V profile? They are a real group, not missing data (F87)
_preregistration.calibration: the two expressions for V must agree to < TOL before any model number is read
_preregistration.deflationary: if the heat-capacity peak predicts T*, then T* costs a handful of forward passes, the ring is redundant for it, and it is EXPLAINED rather than merely reproduced -- registered before the run as the outcome that would matter most
_preregistration.kill: T_peak constant across models -> the predictor has no range and the result is NOT DECIDABLE, not a negative
_preregistration.edge_rule: a V peak landing on either end of T_GRID is REJECTED, not used -- F59's rule applied to a maximum; a cell whose peak is the grid's end has not located one

verdict: CALIBRATION FIRST, and it is exact rather than referential: V has two independent expressions -- Var_{p_T}(z), and T^3 dH/dT by numerical differentiation of the entropy curve -- which are equal analytically. Worst relative disagreement across every model and context measured is 2.30e-03 against a tolerance of 0.02. The implementation reproduces the identity, so V is what the derivation says it is. PRIMARY: over 14 models with a finite T*, the heat-capacity peak and the measured melting temperature correlate at rho = -0.701 (sampled permutation p = 0.0068), mean |T_V - T*| = 1.0351. Unlike F94's, this correlation is interpretable -- correlation_leverage: heat-capacity peak T_V spans 0.6012 against the target's 0.3284 (ratio 1.83, gate 0.5); a correlation is interpretable; distinct_units: 14 sampled T_V values collapse to 11 distinct (gate 4) THE SIGN IS OPPOSITE TO THE NAIVE PREDICTION, and that is recorded rather than explained. V peaks near the logit scale, so a model with more spread-out logits has both a higher T_V and a MORE deterministic conditional at fixed T, which should make its ring attractor survive to a HIGHER temperature. The observed relation runs the other way in both ensembles (settled -0.701, p=0.0068; random -0.741, p=0.0035) with no edge-rejected cells. The registered arm is the settled one. It is logged as a reproducible observation across two independent context ensembles, NOT as a claim: n=14 models, one point per model, no mechanism proposed, and the models are not independent draws -- several share families and corpora, which a per-model permutation null does not account for. F86's own anchor was stated at FAMILY level for exactly that reason. THE DEFLATIONARY OUTCOME DOES NOT FIRE, and that is what protects T*. The peak does not land on T* and is not close to it: T_V occupies [1.21, 1.81] while T* occupies [0.25, 0.58] -- disjoint ranges, mean separation 1.04. So T* is NOT the heat-capacity peak of the model's own conditional, and F86's anchor is not a restatement of next-token entropy response. The ring is not redundant for T*. This is only worth having because the deflationary outcome was written down first as a live possibility, against the strongest static baseline available -- one with a derivation behind it rather than an ad-hoc summary, which is what makes it a stronger version of F92's test.

_note: Tests whether T* -- the melting temperature of the ring's attractor, and the project's only externally-predictive result (F86) -- is derivable from the static conditional via the heat capacity V = Var_{p_T}(z) = T^3 dH/dT that F95's prior-art check turned up in IRIS (arXiv 2607.20860). Logits are temperature-independent, so the whole T grid comes from one forward pass per context. The calibration rung is exact and free: the two expressions for V must agree. Two ensembles because F96 showed a theory's INPUT can be measured off-distribution and invert the reading. Verdict gated by gatecheck.leverage.
